Scenario: Grype skips the folders its settings list at any depth and still reports the project's own

g.text: Given a generated project's API holds the same vulnerable lockfile in its own folder and in
A project generated from the toolbox, with an API under project/api. Its own lockfile, project/api/package-lock.json,
pins lodash 4.17.20, a version with a known vulnerability.
The same lockfile sits in three folders of the API that hold none of its code: .cache, where package managers keep their
downloads, and vendor and venv, where they install libraries.
When the developer scans the project with Grype's settings, it reports the API's own
Grype scans the project with its settings file and saves what it finds as JSON. jq, a JSON reader, then lists the files
There is one: /project/api/package-lock.json, the API's own lockfile. Nothing comes from .cache, vendor or venv.
Then Grype's settings file skips every folder of its list at any depth
The settings file MegaLinter hands Grype. Every folder of its exclude list starts with **/
and ends with /**, like the node_modules line: Grype skips that folder wherever it sits, at
